title: Voltage and Current Water Analogy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A water loop and a robot circuit side by side show that voltage works like water pressure and current works like water flow, using the rule current = voltage / resistance.

educational.topic: Voltage, current, and resistance through the water analogy
learningObjectives: Explain voltage as the push that moves charge, like water pressure
Explain current as the rate of flow of charge, like water flow
Predict how current changes when voltage or resistance changes
Explain why an open loop stops all current
prerequisites: Voltage as pressure and current as flow (Chapter 1: Voltage and Current)
Four 1.5 V AA batteries in series make 6 V (Chapter 1: Voltage and Current)

controls.label: Break the loop / Fix the loop

simulationModel.modelType: Ohm's law with a hydraulic analogy
equations: current = voltage / resistance (0 when the loop is open)
dot speed proportional to current, maximum at 1.2 A
assumptions: The motor behaves like a fixed resistor
Battery voltage does not sag under load
limitations: Real motors draw more current when starting and less when spinning
Water leaks from a broken pipe, but charge does not spill from a broken wire

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Linked sliders driving two matching loops, meters, and a formula line
keyQuestions: What happens to the current if you remove two batteries?
What happens to the current if the motor resistance doubles?
Why do the dots stop everywhere when the loop breaks in one place?
commonMisconceptions: Voltage and current are the same thing
Current gets used up as it goes around the loop
A battery pushes the same current no matter what is connected to it
assessmentOpportunities: Written predictions compared with observed results
Challenge: find settings that give 0.30 A
Exit ticket: two water-analogy reasons a robot's motors run slowly
